[RDSC.9.4] **An unrecognised atom is disposed of by its band, and
skipping is only one of the three answers.** The band of the `oneof`
field number fixes what a loader with no table entry for it must do
([RFCS.16.2]): `256–2047` **skip** — log at info level (category
`dsc-load`, message including the field number and the byte offset)
and step over the frame; `128–255` **reject** with
`DS_ERR_DSC_VERSION`; `1–127` **reject**, the inject band, which no
DSC-legal atom occupies — so an atom there is a misplaced stream
input and the band catches it blind ([RFCS.16.3]). A reader that
*knows* the atom rejects on container-legality instead ([RFCS.17.3]).

So "the loader does not error" holds for the skip band and for
nothing else, and the skip band is where every additive atom is
allocated — which is why a clause citing this one for "a runtime
without an entry for it skips it" is right.
